records.issue_text: AssertEvents.java:isAccessTokenId rejects equality instead of inequality, allowing incorrect grant shortcuts to pass assertions.
records.rationale: The finding is correct. In the isAccessTokenId method at line 485, the condition `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns false when the grant shortcut MATCHES the expected value, which is the opposite of the intended behavior. It should return false when they DON'T match (i.e., use `!equals`). This logic error means the matcher will reject valid token ID

records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java registers grant shortcuts without enforcing the two-character length required for decoding, producing undecodable token IDs for incompatible shortcuts.
records.rationale: The finding identifies a real issue: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() collects shortcuts from OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() without validating they are exactly 2 characters.
